description.narrative: Status of use of the secured Border Management System (sBMS)

comment.narrative: Five officers from the Directorate General of General Security participated in a study visit to Bucharest Romania and Tblisi Georgia in the context of Secured Border Management System sBMS. Officers met with Romanian Border Police officials at the Romanian Border Police Headquarters to discuss the Romanian National EntryExit System and the EU EntryExit system which was still in the development and testing phase. They then observed these systems at Henri Coanda International Airport Bucharest as well as the work of the second line e control office and the forensic laboratory.Officers then travelled to Georgia where the Georgian Ministry of Internal Affairs showcased analytical software Qlik for border crossing data and outlined the Integrated State Border Management Model of Georgia. At Shota Rustaveli Tbilisi International Airport they witnessed the National EntryExit system the second line of the control office and its interface with the first line of the control and then visited the Forensic Laboratory.A second study visit for 3 officers took place to Amsterdam Netherlands 1314 June 2023 the Identity Week Europe Conference in Amsterdam the Netherlands. The twoday conference addressed the latest threats facing Identity as well as cuttingedge technology advancements and opportunities. The conference and exhibition promoted innovation new thinking and more effective identity solutions that Lebanon can be inspired by. The participants also attended a workshop on new trends in cross border crimes on 15 June which included presentations and discussions on new trends in document security fraud and border security. The workshop highlighted how migrant smuggling to Europe is occurring with a focus on identity fraud and new trends in document forgery.

From 2428 April 2023 five officers from the Directorate General of General Security participated in a study visit to Bucharest Romania and Tblisi Georgia in the context of Secured Border Management System sBMS. Officers met with Romanian Border Police officials at the Romanian Border Police Headquarters to discuss the Romanian National EntryExit System and the EU EntryExit system which was still in the development and testing phase. They then observed these systems at Henri Coanda International Airport Bucharest as well as the work of the second line e control office and the forensic laboratory.Officers then travelled to Georgia where the Georgian Ministry of Internal Affairs showcased analytical software Qlik for border crossing data and outlined the Integrated State Border Management Model of Georgia. At Shota Rustaveli Tbilisi International Airport they witnessed the National EntryExit system the second line of the control office and its interface with the first line of the control and then visited the Forensic Laboratory.The followup involved discussions with the Lebanese delegation on lessons learned and designing the new EntryExit system as well as EUD for possible future support. The Entryexit system and the new sBMS will be part of phase 4.A second study visit took place to Amsterdam Netherlands 1314 June 2023. The participants were part of a joint delegation from the EUIBMLBN3 and its IBM sister project funded by NL and both projects are implemented by ICMPD Lebanon. The Action was coorganized and cofinanced by both projects and covered cost for the participation of three LAF representatives namely the Head of the Border Control Committee the Commander of the Land Border Regiments Training School and a trainer on document security in the Identity Week Europe Conference in Amsterdam the Netherlands. The twoday conference hosted more than 200 speakers and addressed the latest threats facing Identity as well as cuttingedge technology advancements and opportunities. The participants also attended a workshop on new trends in cross border crimes on 15 June 2023 which included presentations and discussions on new trends in document security fraud and border security. The workshop highlighted how migrant smuggling to Europe is occurring with a focus on identity fraud and new trends in document forgery.

From 2428 April 2023 five officers from the Directorate General of General Security participated in a study visit to Bucharest Romania and Tblisi Georgia in the context of Secured Border Management System sBMS. Officers met with Romanian Border Police officials at the Romanian Border Police Headquarters to discuss the Romanian National EntryExit System and the EU EntryExit system which was still in the development and testing phase. They then observed these systems at Henri Coanda International Airport Bucharest as well as the work of the second line e control office and the forensic laboratory.Officers then travelled to Georgia where the Georgian Ministry of Internal Affairs showcased analytical software Qlik for border crossing data and outlined the Integrated State Border Management Model of Georgia. At Shota Rustaveli Tbilisi International Airport they witnessed the National EntryExit system the second line of the control office and its interface with the first line of the control and then visited the Forensic Laboratory.The followup involved discussions with the Lebanese delegation on lessons learned and designing the new EntryExit system as well as EUD for possible future support. The Entryexit system and the new sBMS will be part of phase 4.A second study visit took place to Amsterdam Netherlands 1314 June 2023. The participants were part of a joint delegation from the EUIBMLBN3 and its IBM sister project funded by NL and both projects are implemented by ICMPD Lebanon. The Action was coorganized and cofinanced by both projects and covered cost for the participation of three LAF representatives namely the Head of the Border Control Committee the Commander of the Land Border Regiments Training School and a trainer on document security in the Identity Week Europe Conference in Amsterdam the Netherlands. The twoday conference hosted more than 200 speakers and addressed the latest threats facing Identity as well as cuttingedge technology advancements and opportunities. The participants also attended a workshop on new trends in cross border crimes on 15 June 2023 which included presentations and discussions on new trends in document security fraud and border security. The workshop highlighted how migrant smuggling to Europe is occurring with a focus on identity fraud and new trends in document forgery.
